introH2: 🏙️ Why does location matter in Yasothon?
introHtml: Yasothon is a small, compact Isan province — there aren't as many hotels as in big cities, but where you stay still shapes your trip. The city centre (Wari Ratchadet / Witthayatamrong / Prapa roads) is the area within walking distance of Ban Singha Tha, the photogenic old shophouse quarter that's the city's highlight, close to markets and restaurants — ideal for sightseeing and street food. The shopping district on Prachasamphan Road sits near malls and shops with easy access. Meanwhile the edge of town and the bypass road suit self-drivers — easy in and out of the city, big car parks, and close to Phaya Thaen Park where the famous Rocket Festival is held. If you come during the Rocket Festival in May, book well ahead — city rooms fill fast and prices jump. This guide rounds up 12 Yasothon hotels we've already reviewed across every tier, with real guest-review feedback, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Yasothon has no metro and no train station in town — getting around is mostly by car, with most visitors arriving by coach at the bus terminal or driving in. City-centre stays put you within walking distance of Ban Singha Tha, markets and restaurants, ideal if you don't have a car (The Zen, The Green Park Grand, The Colour, JP Emerald, RP City). Bypass / edge-of-town stays need a car or Grab but offer easy access and big car parks (The Model Garden, Crystal, Zigzag, Vimanmek). The stay behind the bus terminal is walkable to coach bays, ideal if you arrive by bus (Big Elephant). The areas in this guide: City Centre — Ban Singha Tha, markets, food; Shopping District — malls, shops; Edge of Town–Bypass — easy driving, near Phaya Thaen Park.

entries.name: U-Sabai Villa Yasothon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In-town Yasothon · Soi Chaeng Sanit 1 · quiet garden
entries.addr: 28 Soi Chaeng Sanit 1, Nai Mueang, Mueang Yasothon
entries.storyHtml: U-Sabai Villa Yasothon is the top-scoring stay in this guide at 9.7 — a minimalist boutique villa that opened in 2024 with just 8 rooms. It sits on Soi Chaeng Sanit 1, central but tucked deep enough into a garden to stay quiet. Real guest reviews praise the brand-new, spotless rooms, warm minimalist design, comfortable beds, free breakfast and owners who look after you like you're staying with friends. The flip side: it's tiny at 8 rooms, with no pool, no lift, and rooms book out fast. Best for couples or solo travellers who value newness, cleanliness and a quiet atmosphere.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 8 rooms, book early — especially around the May Rocket Festival. Ask for a room with a balcony or private terrace facing the garden for the best vibe. Take the free breakfast, then drive into town to wander Ban Singha Tha.

Warm minimalist design, spotless, comfortable beds
Free breakfast · quiet garden, hands-on friendly owners

entries.name: The Green Park Grand Yasothon
entries.addr: 209/12 Wari Ratchadet Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Yasothon
entries.storyHtml: The Green Park Grand Yasothon is the biggest and most-reviewed hotel in this guide — 240 reviews — and the only place in Yasothon with an indoor pool and fitness centre, scoring 8.7. It sits in the city centre on Wari Ratchadet Road, walkable to Ban Singha Tha and the markets. Real guest reviews value its full-hotel feel — rare in a small town — with the pool, gym, big car park and central location. Be aware that old-wing rooms feel dated; reviewers suggest asking for the main building or a renovated room. Best for families, conference and seminar guests, and anyone who wants a pool in Yasothon.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Old-wing rooms are cheaper but older — if you want newer, ask for a Deluxe/VIP in the main building and view the room first. It's a popular conference hotel, so it fills fast during big events or the Rocket Festival. Use the indoor pool even when it's blazing outside.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Yasothon hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in Yasothon?
faq.a: Yasothon is a small city with 3 main areas. City centre (Wari Ratchadet / Witthayatamrong / Prapa roads) is walkable to the Ban Singha Tha old quarter, markets and restaurants — ideal for sightseeing and those without a car (The Zen, The Green Park Grand, The Colour, JP Emerald). The shopping district is near malls and shops (RP City). Edge of town / bypass offers easy access and big car parks, ideal for self-drivers (Crystal, The Model Garden, Zigzag, Vimanmek).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Yasothon hotels cost?
faq.a: Rates in Yasothon are fairly low versus big tourist cities: budget stays from around ฿450–700/night (BM Grand, The Colour, Zigzag, Vimanmek, Big Elephant, The Model Garden), and mid-range to 4-star hotels and boutiques around ฿650–1,200 (The Zen, The Green Park Grand, Crystal, U-Sabai Villa, RP City, JP Emerald). All prices are approximate starting rates for a standard room; during the May Rocket Festival rates run higher and rooms fill fast.

faq.q: ❓ Which Yasothon hotel has the best score?
faq.a: U-Sabai Villa tops the list at 9.7 — a boutique villa opened in 2024, with brand-new clean rooms and free breakfast. Behind it, Crystal Hotel and RP City score 9.0, and The Zen Hotel 8.9, a boutique walkable to Ban Singha Tha. The Green Park Grand scores 8.7 but has by far the most reviews (240) and is the only hotel in town with a pool, so it's the pick if you want solid data and full facilities.

faq.q: ❓ Which Yasothon hotel has a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yasothon is a small town and pools are scarce. The Green Park Grand Yasothon ฿650 is the main option with an indoor pool and fitness centre — a 100+ room, 4-star hotel in the city centre and the most reviewed in this guide at 240. It's ideal for families and conference guests; if you want newer rooms, ask for the main building or a renovated room.

faq.q: ❓ Is Yasothon easy to get around without a car?
faq.a: Yasothon has no metro and no in-town train station; most people arrive by coach at the bus terminal or drive in. Without a car, staying central is easiest — walkable to Ban Singha Tha, markets and restaurants (The Zen, The Green Park Grand, The Colour, JP Emerald) — or stay at Big Elephant Hotel behind the bus terminal, walkable to the coach bays. Edge-of-town / bypass stays really need a car or Grab.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book for the Yasothon Rocket Festival?
faq.a: The Yasothon Rocket Festival runs in May at Phaya Thaen Park — a major festival that draws crowds into town, so city rooms fill very fast and prices rise. Book weeks to months ahead. Leave it late and you may only find edge-of-town stays that need a car. Compare 3 sites (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) before booking — each review page in this guide has the price-comparison links.
